title: Iowa Western students record 5 EVPs in first paranormal investigation at Bregant House
excerpt: We are just a few days away from Halloween, and some Iowa Western students have spent the month digging into the spookiest places in Council Bluffs.
content:
Iowa Western students probe first paranormal investigation at Council Bluffs' Bregant House

COUNCIL BLUFFS, Iowa —

We are just a few days away from Halloween, and some Iowa Western students have spent the month digging into the spookiest places in Council Bluffs.

They even conducted the first-ever paranormal investigation at the historic Bregant House.

It's Iowa Western's new paranormal course called Haunted Bluffs. It's a continued education course, so the class doesn't count for credit but is open for all to join.

"This just kind of popped in my head at the paranormal piece to learn about that and then actually maybe experience some haunted history sort of thing," Josh Baker, the professor of the course and the Continuing Education Coordinator at Iowa Western Community College.

"This is the second one that we've taken," said Demi Rushlow, one of the students in Baker's class. Rushlow said she's taken a class at another college before, but this one is her favorite.

During the first meeting of the course, the group dove into the history of each site.

"We went to the squirrel cage, and we went to the Rail Museum. We are now at Bregant House and then the cemetery. And each one has different stories that make it so that you kind of want to go see if there's anything else there," Rushlow said.

They also learned about all the tools they would use during their investigations.

"The box, the temperature meter, the voice recorders, EMF, all that fun stuff. We got to play with the toys," Rushlow said.

After learning the background knowledge on each of the sites and figuring out how to use their gear, the group tackled the physical investigation.

KETV joined the class' third investigation at the Bregant House in Council Bluffs.

"It was built in 1912 for its owners, Jean and Inez Breck. They were both vaudeville performers. They actually met at Coney Island," Corrine Peterson, the Director of Programs and Development for the Pottawattamie County Historical Society, said.

Peterson said Jean died in the 1940s and Inez died in 1969.

"Inez was 3.5ft tall, and Jean was 3.75ft tall," Peterson said.

It was the first ever paranormal investigation at what many call the doll house.

"I don't think anybody has ever been in here long enough to maybe even try to experience anything," Baker said.

"You just feel there's a difference in the air. I don't know that there's anything in this one," Rushlow said.

One week after their investigation of the Bregant house, the class met to look through the evidence.

They recorded five electronic voice phenomena, or EVPs, from the investigation.

"That is where, you have like a digital recorder, you will ask a question, and then when you play it back, you'll actually hear a response or a noise," Baker said.

One track they played sounded like someone was sighing.

"It's either a very low kind of sigh, that was real weird," Baker said.

If you're brave enough, Baker hopes to offer the class again in the spring.

"I'm going to try to maybe incorporate several other locations to kind of keep it fresh and new, but obviously, if you've never did an experience like this, it's going to be fun," Baker said.
